summary: Artifact-first review combines the asynchronous operating loop with a common evidence envelope whose depth can be tuned to risk.

items.text: Consume diffs, checks, evidence and risk notes through Trust Layer; Fire, Track, Review defines when humans look, while the layer defines what trustworthy evidence is available.
Compose the asynchronous review hand-off with YOLO with Rails so unattended execution ends at a deliberate artifact-and-evidence review point.
Review the compact evidence envelope first and drill into the raw run trace only when claims conflict, evidence is missing or the result is suspicious.
For bug fixes, require the minimal patch together with its reproduced-red and proven-green unit-test evidence.
Require every quality-gate agent to emit the same verdict, evidence, confidence, waiver and remediation fields.
Render a compact top-level verdict from a richer machine-readable analysis report rather than duplicating evidence.
Attach a risk class and review contract at dispatch: required tests, prohibited paths, evidence to capture, maximum cost, and the person or role authorized to accept.
Use bounded concurrency and review-queue backpressure so new work is not fired when completed artifacts already exceed reviewer capacity.
Route tasks using measured capability by task type, then feed accepted, revised, rejected and regressed outcomes back into that map.
See Plan-First Agents for the related use case or counterpoint: Plan first, type second. Expensive decisions live in the plan.

See Skip the Pull Request for the related use case or counterpoint: In agent-first delivery, gates in front of the integration merge replace the human pull-request review — the operator reads verdicts, not diffs.
